memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If what a prophet proclaims in the name of the Lord does not take place or come true, that is a message the Lord has not spoken. That prophet has spoken presumptuously, so do not be alarmed. - Deut 18:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives His people a clear test, if a prophet claims to speak for the Lord, but what he says does not come true, then the Lord did not speak through him. A true word from God always proves reliable. And God adds a gentle reassurance, "do not be alarmed." His people did not need to live in fear of every bold claim or frightening prediction.

This is such practical kindness from God. The world is full of loud, confident voices making sweeping claims, and it can be tempting to feel anxious or shaken by them. But God gives His people a way to weigh these voices and a reason not to be afraid. Truth stands the test; falsehood eventually collapses.

The same steadiness is ours in Christ. We do not need to be alarmed by every doomsday prediction, every self-proclaimed prophet, or every confident but false teaching. God's Word is the standard, and it never fails. When Jesus warned of false prophets, He told us to know them by their fruit (Matt 7:15-16). We can live with calm hearts, anchored in the sure Word of God rather than tossed about by every claim. What frightening or confident voice do you need to weigh against God's truth, so that you can stop being alarmed and rest in Him?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What loud or fearful voices have unsettled you lately?
2. How does measuring them against God's Word bring peace?
3. Where do you need to rest in God's reliable truth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your Word always proves true. Anchor my heart in Your truth, so I need not be alarmed by false voices. Amen.
